cards.name: Unsharp Mask
cards.summary: Sharpens by boosting contrast along edges (image minus a blurred copy). Small radius = fine detail sharpening; large radius with low amount = local-contrast 'clarity' punch.
use_for: crisp up soft archival or AI-upscaled footage in documentaries
add bite to press photos used as full-screen stills in news reels
large-radius, low-amount clarity pass on flat b-roll for trailers
restore perceived detail after downscaling 4K sources to 1080
avoid: high Amount with a small Radius exaggerates compression blocks and noise in web-sourced news clips
white/dark halos around faces and on-screen text at high Amount + Radius
do not sharpen before a scale-up or zoom; sharpen last in the stack

params.name: Amount
params.does: Sharpening strength in percent (default 0 = no change). Negative values push the other way (softening); unverified.
params.typical: 50-120 for detail; 20-40 with a big Radius for clarity

params.name: Radius
params.does: Distance in pixels over which edge contrast is boosted.

params.name: Threshold
params.does: Minimum edge difference that gets sharpened, normalised 0..1; protects flat areas, skin and noise.

params.name: Color Mode
params.does: 0/1 switch (Premiere's copy of this effect exposes it as a true/false checkbox); meaning unverified, probably luminance-only vs per-channel sharpening.

cards.scripting: Match name is the updated 'ADBE Unsharp Mask2'. Amount defaults to 0, so nothing shows until it is set. Threshold is normalised 0..1 here (the legacy effect used 0-255 levels). Color Mode is a 0/1 switch whose meaning is not confirmed; leave at 0. Put it after Transform/scale effects so halos are not rescaled. Premiere's Unsharp Mask has the same four controls (Amount -500..500, Radius, Threshold 0..1, Color Mode as a boolean). The old 'ADBE Unsharp Mask' (Threshold 0-255) is in the obsolete bin; do not use it for new work.

verified.note: Edges and local contrast are clearly crisper than the reference (stripes, faces, foreground-block rims) with light halos, as described.

cards.name: Mocha AE
cards.summary: Boris FX planar tracker bundled with After Effects: you open the separate Mocha AE window to track a flat surface or roto a shape, then the effect applies that tracked shape as a matte or exports corner-pin / transform data to another layer.
use_for: replace a phone, TV or billboard screen in news b-roll with a graphic
track a blur matte over a face or number plate for privacy
pin a label or lower-third onto a moving wall or banner in documentaries
isolate a tracked region (a speaker's face, a product) on a duplicate layer with Apply Matte for a local colour or exposure fix
avoid: cannot be driven headless: tracking happens in the Mocha GUI, so an automated pipeline can only reuse an existing track
planar tracks fail on occluded or textureless surfaces (plain walls, blown-out screens)
stabilisation is a Mocha Pro module, not part of Mocha AE; use Warp Stabilizer for shaky footage

params.name: Apply Matte
params.does: 0/1: cuts the layer to the matte from the Mocha track.
params.typical: 1 when using the track as a mask

params.name: View Matte
params.does: 0/1: shows the matte as black and white for checking.

params.name: Feather
params.does: Softens the matte edge in pixels.

params.name: Dilate
params.does: Grows (+) or shrinks (-) the matte.

params.name: Invert Mask
params.does: 0/1: inverts the matte (keep everything except the tracked shape).

params.name: Export Option
params.does: Type of tracking data the Create Track Data button writes: 1 Corner Pin, 2 Corner Pin (Support Motion Blur), 3 Transform (read from After Effects 26.0).

params.name: Layer Export To
params.does: Layer reference that receives the exported corner-pin/transform data.

params.name: Top Left
params.does: Tracked corner-pin point in comp pixels (also Top Right, Bottom Left, Bottom Right, Center).
params.typical: written by Mocha; do not hand-set

cards.scripting: 'mocha Arb Data 0/1' are custom blobs holding the Mocha project and tracks and cannot be set from a spec; 'Launch Mocha AE' and the Create Track Data control are UI buttons. A script can only toggle Apply Matte / Feather / Dilate / Invert Mask on a layer that already carries track data (e.g. from a saved preset or template). Layer Export To and Right View are layer references. Corner points are comp pixels [x, y]. 'First parameter', 'Last parameter' and 'License Control' are internal. Premiere has no Mocha effect; its built-in mask tracking is the closest.

verified.note: Card status is needs_input, so no gallery frame was rendered.

cards.name: Arithmetic
cards.summary: Runs a simple math operation (Xor, Add, Difference, Slice, Multiply...) between every pixel's red, green and blue values and constant values you set per channel, giving hard colour casts, channel inversions and solarised looks.
use_for: per-channel colour flip for glitch / 'hacker' segments in AI-education explainers
one- or two-frame solarised flash on an impact beat in trailers
Slice operator for a hard poster look behind titles
avoid: looks cheap and digital on faces; not a grading tool
Clipping 0 lets values wrap and produces noisy bands

params.name: Operator
params.does: The math operation (1-based popup, see enum_labels).
params.typical: 6 Difference to invert a channel; 4 Add / 5 Subtract for casts

params.name: Red Value
params.does: Constant applied to the red channel, 8-bit levels.
params.typical: 255 with Difference = invert red; 40-120 with Add for a cast

params.name: Green Value
params.does: Constant applied to the green channel.

params.name: Blue Value
params.does: Constant applied to the blue channel.

params.name: Clipping
params.does: 1 clips results to 0-255; 0 lets them wrap.

cards.scripting: Default Operator 3 (Xor) with all values 0 is an identity, so it shows nothing until values change. Values are 8-bit levels 0-255 regardless of project bit depth. Operator labels (enum_labels) are read from After Effects 26.0. Premiere v26 has no Arithmetic effect (absent from the harvested Premiere list); there use Invert, or Lumetri Color for casts.

verified.note: Red channel is inverted (Difference 255): white background turns cyan, navy areas turn red, red stripes go dark; a hard channel-flip look as described.

cards.name: Blend
cards.summary: Blends the layer with another layer picked in the effect, using Crossfade, Color Only, Tint Only, Darken Only or Lighten Only.
use_for: Color Only with a solid or gradient layer to colourise footage in brand colours (takes per-pixel hue/saturation from the other layer)
Darken Only / Lighten Only merge of a texture plate (paper, smoke) into archival footage
crossfade two layers inside one precomp without a transition
avoid: the other layer is read without its effects and masks; precompose it first
usually cleaner with layer blend modes or track mattes

params.name: Blend With Layer
params.does: Layer reference to blend with (default None).

params.name: Mode
params.does: How the two layers combine (1-based, see enum_labels).

params.name: Blend With Original
params.does: Mix back toward the untouched layer; Adobe documents that at 100% the effect has no visible result. Harvested as 0..1 with default 1, so set it toward 0 to see the blend.

params.name: If Layer Sizes Differ
params.does: 1 Center, 2 Stretch to Fit.

cards.scripting: Blend With Layer is a layer reference; with None (0) the effect does nothing, so a second layer must exist in the comp. Blend With Original is harvested as 0..1 with default 1; if that means 100% original the effect is invisible until it is lowered toward 0. Unconfirmed: verify on the render. Premiere v26 has no Blend effect (absent from the harvested Premiere list); stack the clips and use the top clip's Opacity blend mode instead.

verified.note: Card status is needs_input, so no gallery frame was rendered.

cards.name: CC Composite
cards.summary: Composites the layer's original, pre-effect image (or another layer picked in Top Layer) back over the result of the effects above it, using a transfer mode and opacity. Mixes a stylise effect with the clean image, or self-blends the layer for punchier contrast.
use_for: after Glow, Find Edges or Cartoon, lay the clean footage back on top at 30-70% for a controlled stylised look
self-multiply or overlay for quick punch on flat archival clips
bring back detail over a blurred or distorted pass in trailer looks
avoid: first in the stack with the default mode it changes nothing
Transfer Mode indices count menu separators (4, 10, 17, 25, 29, 34, 39): pick the index of a label in enum_labels

params.name: Transfer Mode
params.does: Blend mode used to put the original back on top (1-based popup, 41 indices, default 3 = In Front). The menu (read from After Effects 26.0) counts separators: 1 Copy, 2 Behind, 3 In front, 5 Darken, 6 Multiply, 7 Linear Burn ... 11 Add, 12 Lighten, 13 Screen ... 18 Overlay, 19 Soft Light ... 26 Difference ... 41 Luminescent Premul (enum_labels).

params.name: Opacity
params.does: Strength of the original image on top.

params.name: RGB Only
params.does: 1 keeps the effected layer's alpha; 0 also composites alpha.

params.name: Top Layer
params.does: Layer reference for the image put on top; defaults to the layer itself.

cards.scripting: Stack order matters: it uses the image as it was before ALL effects above it. Top Layer is a layer reference that defaults to the layer itself (harvest default 1); leave it. Transfer Mode is not animatable; its default 3 is In Front (plain composite, identity when CC Composite is first in the stack). The demo value 6 is Multiply (read from After Effects 26.0; the render shows the self-multiply); Screen is 13 and Overlay 18, not 7 and 8. Use match 'CS Composite'; 'CC Composite' is the obsolete twin (its popup is named 'Composite Original'). No Premiere equivalent.

verified.note: Self-blend with Transfer Mode 6 clearly darkens and deepens the whole frame (mean level 168 -> 105), consistent with a self-Multiply contrast boost.

cards.name: Calculations
cards.summary: Combines one channel of this layer with a channel of a second layer through a blend mode. Used alone, it pulls a single channel (Gray, Red, Green, Blue, Alpha) out as a black-and-white image.
use_for: punchy B&W from the red channel for archival or flashback looks in documentaries
extract a channel as a luma matte for sky or smoke compositing
blend a texture or second plate in by blend mode for trailers
avoid: the second layer is read without its effects and masks; precompose
Gray conversion is flat; grade afterwards with Curves/Levels

params.name: Input Channel
params.does: Which channel of this layer is used (see enum_labels).
params.typical: 3 Red for dramatic B&W; 2 Gray for neutral mono

params.name: Invert Input
params.does: 0/1: inverts the input channel.

params.name: Second Layer
params.does: Layer reference for the second source (defaults to this layer).

params.name: Second Layer Channel
params.does: Which channel of the second layer is used.

params.name: Second Layer Opacity
params.does: Opacity of the second layer, harvested on a 0..1 scale (UI shows %); Adobe: 0% means the second layer has no influence.

params.name: Blending Mode
params.does: Blend mode between the two (1-based, 37 indices including separators at 3, 8, 14, 21, 25, 30, 35; labels in enum_labels (read from After Effects 26.0)).
params.typical: leave 1 unless blending a second layer

params.name: Preserve Transparency
params.does: 0/1: keeps the original alpha.

cards.scripting: Second Layer Opacity is harvested on a 0..1 scale (UI shows a percentage); at 0 only Input Channel drives the result, which is how the single-channel B&W works with no second layer. Second Layer is a layer reference defaulting to the layer itself. Blending Mode indices count menu separators; the labels are in enum_labels (read from After Effects 26.0). Premiere v26 has no Calculations effect (absent from the harvested Premiere list); use Black & White or Lumetri Color for mono looks there.

verified.note: Frame is a single-channel black-and-white image that matches the reference red channel best (corr 0.92 vs 0.82 green), so Input Channel 3 = Red B&W as described.

cards.name: Channel Combiner
cards.summary: Maps one channel or a colour-space conversion (e.g. Lightness, Hue, RGB to HLS, RGB to YUV) into a target channel, producing channel swaps, false colour or single-channel greyscale.
use_for: short false-colour flashes for glitch transitions in reels
extract hue, saturation or lightness as a greyscale matte for compositing
copy luminance into alpha to make a quick luma matte
avoid: RGB/HLS/YUV conversions look garish on skin; keep them to brief stylised beats
the From / To menus count separators as indices (From 6, 11, 17; To 5, 9, 14): take an index from enum_labels and never set a separator

params.name: From
params.does: Source channel or conversion (1-based popup, 19 indices incl. separators). Documented items include multichannel conversions (RGB to HLS, HLS to RGB, RGB to YUV, YUV to RGB, straight/premultiplied alpha conversions) and single sources (Red, Green, Blue, Alpha, Lightness, Hue, Saturation, Luminance, Saturation Multiplied, Min RGB, Max RGB); the menu (read from After Effects 26.0): 1 RGB to HLS, 2 HLS to RGB, 3 RGB to YUV, 4 YUV to RGB, 5 Straight to Premultiplied, 7 Red, 8 Green, 9 Blue, 10 Alpha, 12 Hue, 13 Lightness, 14 Luminance, 15 Saturation, 16 Saturation Multiplied, 18 Min RGB, 19 Max RGB (6, 11 and 17 are separators).
params.typical: a conversion for false colour, a single channel for mattes

params.name: To
params.does: Destination for single-channel sources: Red Only, Green Only, Blue Only, Alpha Only, Hue Only, Lightness Only, Saturation Only and similar (menu (read from After Effects 26.0): 1 Red, 2 Green, 3 Blue, 4 Alpha, 6 Hue, 7 Lightness (default), 8 Saturation, 10-13 Red / Green / Blue / Alpha only, 15-17 Hue / Lightness / Saturation only; 5, 9 and 14 are separators). Ignored by the multichannel conversions.

params.name: Invert
params.does: 0/1: inverts (1 minus) the output channel values.

params.name: Solid Alpha
params.does: 0/1: forces a fully opaque alpha.
params.typical: 1 when the result must stay opaque

params.name: Use 2nd Layer
params.does: 0/1: take the source from Source Layer instead of this layer.

params.name: Source Layer
params.does: Layer reference used when Use 2nd Layer = 1.

cards.scripting: From (19) and To (17) popups count menu separators as indices; the labels are in enum_labels (read from After Effects 26.0); the demo uses only Invert, the setting that was rendered. Source Layer is a layer reference that only matters when Use 2nd Layer = 1. Adobe's tip: any channel as greyscale = that channel in From + Lightness Only in To (e.g. From 7 Red, To 16). No Premiere equivalent: Premiere v26 has no Channel Mixer, and its 'Channel Mix' effect only scales or inverts channels, it cannot route one channel into another.

verified.note: Strong inverted false-colour result (magenta/cyan/blue psychedelic palette) replaces the natural colours, matching the false-colour look.

cards.name: Compound Arithmetic
cards.summary: Combines this layer with a second source layer by a math operator (Add, Multiply, Difference, Screen, Overlay...) on RGB, ARGB or alpha. With the layer itself as source it gives a quick self-blend.
use_for: screen a light-leak or fire plate into footage for trailers
multiply a paper or dust texture into archival documentary footage
self-overlay (default source = itself) for instant punch on flat clips
difference against an offset precomp of itself for edge/glitch looks
avoid: the second source is read without its effects and masks
Overflow Wrap produces harsh banding
Adobe keeps it only for compatibility with old projects and it is 8-bpc; layer blend modes do the same faster and in 16/32 bpc

params.name: Second Source Layer
params.does: Layer reference to combine with (defaults to this layer).

params.name: Operator
params.does: Math/blend operator (see enum_labels).
params.typical: 13 Screen for light leaks, 4 Multiply for textures, 14 Overlay for punch

params.name: Operate on Channels
params.does: 1 RGB, 2 ARGB, 3 Alpha.

params.name: Overflow Behavior
params.does: 1 Clip, 2 Wrap, 3 Scale.

params.name: Stretch Second Source to Fit
params.does: 0/1: scale the second source to this layer's size.

params.name: Blend With Original
params.does: Mix back toward the untouched layer, percent.

cards.scripting: Second Source Layer is a layer reference; harvest default 1 = the layer itself, which is why the demo self-overlay shows a change with no extra layer. Default Operator 1 (Copy) of itself is an identity. Operator labels are read from After Effects 26.0 (9 and 10 are named Lighter and Darker there). Premiere v26 has no Compound Arithmetic (absent from the harvested Premiere list); use the clip's Opacity blend mode.

verified.note: Self-Overlay gives a visible punch: whites brighter, darks deeper, colours richer (contrast std 51 -> 71) with no other change.

cards.name: Invert
cards.summary: Inverts a chosen channel or colour space: full RGB photo negative, hue flip, lightness/luminance flip, or alpha inversion.
use_for: 1-3 frame negative flash on a beat or impact in trailers and reels
x-ray/negative look for a 'hidden document revealed' moment in explainers
Hue (7) for a surreal colour flip that keeps exposure
Alpha (16) to flip a matte
avoid: long full-negative stretches tire the eye and add flashing-content risk
full negatives on faces read as horror; keep them short

params.name: Channel
params.does: What gets inverted (see enum_labels; 5, 10, 15 are menu separators).
params.typical: 1 RGB for a negative, 7 Hue for colour flip

params.name: Blend With Original
params.does: Mix back toward the original, percent.
params.typical: 0 for the flash; 50-70 for a washed half-negative

cards.scripting: Default Channel 1 = RGB, so the effect is fully visible as soon as it is applied. Channel indices count menu separators: 5, 10 and 15 are separators and must not be set. For a flash, keyframe Blend With Original rather than toggling the effect. Premiere's Invert has the same menu but its Channel control is 0-based there (harvested 0-15), so subtract 1 when porting an index.

verified.note: Full RGB photo negative of the reference: faces dark blue-grey, dark clothing cream, red stripes green.

cards.name: Minimax
cards.summary: Replaces each pixel with the minimum or maximum value found within a radius, spreading bright or dark areas into blocky shapes; on alpha it grows or chokes a matte.
use_for: choke or spread a keyed/alpha matte by 1-3 px (Channel Alpha)
thicken thin text or line art so it survives small phone screens
stylised blocky light-spread on night city shots in trailers
avoid: large radius on footage gives obvious square blocks
Maximum on Color brightens and destroys detail

params.name: Operation
params.does: 1 Minimum (shrink brights), 2 Maximum (spread brights), 3 Minimum then Maximum, 4 Maximum then Minimum.

params.name: Radius
params.does: Size of the search area in pixels.

params.name: Channel
params.does: Which channels are processed (see enum_labels).
params.typical: 6 Alpha for matte work, 1 Color for looks

params.name: Direction
params.does: 1 Horizontal & Vertical, 2 Just Horizontal, 3 Just Vertical.

params.name: Don't Shrink Edges
params.does: 0/1: stops the result pulling in from the layer edges.

cards.scripting: Radius defaults to 0 (no change). Cost grows with Radius. Channel labels are read from After Effects 26.0. No Premiere equivalent.

verified.note: Bright areas spread into blocky 12 px squares over darker detail (faces, flowers, foreground blocks), the painterly maximum spread described.

cards.name: Remove Color Matting
cards.summary: Removes the dark or coloured fringe on semi-transparent edges of a layer whose alpha was premultiplied against a background colour (e.g. graphics rendered on black).
use_for: clean black halos on logo or graphic renders imported with the wrong alpha interpretation
fix fringe on soft-edged elements (fire, smoke, light leaks) rendered over black
avoid: does nothing on fully opaque footage
a wrong Background Color makes edges worse

params.name: Background Color
params.does: The colour the alpha was premultiplied with.

params.name: Clipping
params.does: 0/1: clip HDR values, i.e. clamp over-range results (matters in 32-bpc projects).

cards.scripting: Only semi-transparent pixels change, so it needs a layer with a real alpha channel (graphic, keyed or masked layer); an opaque full-frame plate shows nothing. Harvested default colour has alpha 0; set Background Color explicitly, e.g. '#000000'. Interpreting the footage as Premultiplied in the project is often the better fix.

verified.note: Card status is needs_input, so no gallery frame was rendered.

cards.name: Set Channels
cards.summary: Rebuilds the red, green, blue and alpha channels from chosen channels (or luminance, hue, lightness, saturation) of up to four source layers, defaulting to the layer itself; used for channel swaps and channel-based mattes.
use_for: swap red and blue for an eerie false-colour flashback or 'alternate reality' beat
copy luminance into alpha (Set Alpha to Luminance) to make a luma matte for smoke or light-leak overlays
build a stylised channel-split glitch frame in reels
avoid: channel swaps on faces look alien; keep to short stylised beats
source layers are read without their effects and masks

params.name: Set Red To Source 1’s
params.does: Which channel of Source Layer 1 becomes red (see enum_labels).

params.name: Set Green To Source 2’s
params.does: Which channel of Source Layer 2 becomes green.

params.name: Set Blue To Source 3’s
params.does: Which channel of Source Layer 3 becomes blue.

params.name: Set Alpha To Source 4’s
params.does: Which channel of Source Layer 4 becomes alpha.
params.typical: 5 Luminance for a luma matte; 9 Full to force opaque

params.name: Source Layer 1
params.does: Layer reference feeding red (0 = None = this layer); Source Layer 2-4 work the same.

params.name: If Layer Sizes Differ
params.does: 0/1: stretch source layers to fit.

cards.scripting: Property names use a typographic apostrophe (U+2019), e.g. 'Set Red To Source 1’s'; a plain ' will not match. Source Layer 1-4 are layer references; default 0 = None = use this layer, so channel swaps work with no extra layer. Defaults (1,2,3,4) are an identity. All ten options (1 Red, 2 Green, 3 Blue, 4 Alpha, 5 Luminance, 6 Hue, 7 Lightness, 8 Saturation, 9 Full, 10 Off) are read from After Effects 26.0. Premiere v26 has no Set Channels or Channel Mixer; its 'Channel Mix' only scales or inverts channels and cannot swap them.

verified.note: Red and blue are swapped: red stripes turn blue, navy areas turn brown, maroon foreground blocks turn purple, as described.
